text: Slabs distribute loads from floors and transfer them to beams and columns in reinforced concrete structures.
Beam reinforcement is designed to resist bending moments and shear forces caused by structural loads.
Columns primarily carry axial loads from beams and slabs down to the foundation.
Footings spread structural loads from columns into a larger soil area to prevent settlement failure.
Foundations transfer building loads safely into the ground based on soil bearing capacity.
Load distribution in RCC structures follows the path slab → beam → column → footing → soil.
Reinforcement bars in beams are placed at tension zones to resist bending stress effectively.
Shear stress in beams increases near supports and must be handled with stirrups.
Differential settlement occurs when different parts of the foundation settle unevenly due to soil variation.
Proper column grid alignment ensures uniform load transfer and prevents structural imbalance.
